prerequisites: Fundamental knowledge from (engineering) mathematics: arithmetic operations with fractions, complex numbers, differential and integral calculus, ordinary linear differential equations of the first order with constant coefficients, Taylor series, polynomials, rational functions, partial fraction decomposition.

learning_outcomes.text: The participants will be familiarized with the fundamental mathematical tools for dealing with control systems.
Participants can use these tools for the analysis of systems and control loops as well as for the design of controllers.

syllabus_topics: Linearization of ordinary nonlinear first-order differential equations and systems of differential equations
Ordinary linear first-order differential equations with constant coefficients

Application of the Laplace transformation to ordinary linear first-order differential equations with constant coefficients, transfer function, poles and zeros, convolution integral, stability, frequency response
Linear time-invariant systems, modeling, typical transfer elements (P-, I-, D-, PT1-, PT2(S), DT1-, PD-, Tt-element), all-pass elements, minimum-phase and non-minimum-phase behavior
Closed control loop, requirements, stability, Nyquist criterion
Controller design, classification of methods, standard controllers (PID controllers), frequency response methods, algebraic/analytical controller design (pole placement in the standard control loop)
Approximate conversion of a continuous control algorithm (differential equation, transfer function) into a discrete-time control algorithm (difference equation)
Selected aspects of control engineering, e.g., digital control (if applicable)
teaching_methods: Practice problems and supplementary materials as text documents
assessment_rules: The module examination is either a written exam or an oral examination. The conduct and duration of the examination are in accordance with the applicable examination regulations. This examination accounts for 100% of the module grade.
bibliography: An up-to-date bibliography is included in the provided lecture materials.
